site.name: forge-coder
site.summary: Forge Coder — agentic coding IDE (local demo) Fictional agentic coding product. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Agent run view Three-pane IDE-style layout: file tree (left) + agent chat (center) + live diff preview (right). Left — file tree: - Virtual TypeScript project (`atlas-cli`) with folder collapse, file-status badges (M for modified, + for newly added), and a summary footer. - Clicking any file marked M / + loads its diff into the right pane.

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the single-page Forge Coder agent run interface, validating the core agent-review workflow across the file tree, chat timeline, diff preview, and run controls, plus adjacent navigation and action surfaces on desktop and mobile.
run_plan.summary: The run should center on the visible primary flow: reviewing an in-progress coding task, inspecting changed files from the tree, switching diff views, and deciding whether to respond, interrupt, rerun, open the editor, or accept changes. Because only index.html is known, exploration should go deep within this one-page app rather than hunting for separate pages. Adjacent checks should probe top navigation, repo/editor actions, composer controls, and whether file/status interactions keep the three-pane context coherent. Mobile coverage should focus on usability of the dense header, small tap targets, pane accessibility, and whether critical actions remain reachable.
assumptions: Only index.html is confirmed in prescan, so navigation items like Agent, Inbox, Runs, and Settings may swap in-page states rather than load separate HTML files.
The main task state is an active run (#243) with visible modified/new files, timeline events, and a diff preview already loaded.
Files marked M or + are intended to be selectable and should update the right diff pane.
Unified/Split are diff-mode toggles for the current file preview.
Reply textarea, Auto-apply edits, and Send form a request-to-agent interaction path.
risk_hotspots: index.html: file tree selection for modified/new files may fail to sync with the diff preview
index.html: Unified/Split diff toggle may not preserve file context or render correctly
index.html: Accept all changes is a high-impact action with potential missing confirmation or unclear state change
index.html: Interrupt and Rerun are competing run controls that may be ambiguous during an active run
index.html: reply composer with Auto-apply edits checkbox may create risky submission behavior
index.html: top nav links (Agent, Inbox, Runs, Settings) may look navigational but be non-functional or weakly differentiated
index.html: Connect a repo / Open in VS Code / Open editor actions may be dead ends or unclear in a local demo
index.html mobile: dense three-pane IDE layout and many small tap targets create high usability risk

phases.title: Baseline run-state mapping
phases.objective: Establish how the single-page interface is organized and confirm the default active-run state before deeper interaction.
key_checks: Confirm the three-pane structure: file tree, agent conversation/timeline, and diff preview.
Record which navigation item appears active and whether run metadata is clearly understandable.
Verify visible action groups in the header and run toolbar: Interrupt, Rerun, Open editor, Accept all changes, Connect a repo, Open in VS Code.
Check whether the currently selected file in the tree matches the diff header in the right pane.
Inspect whether the conversation timeline communicates progress, file reads/edits, and test execution clearly.
exit_criteria: The active state and hierarchy of the page are documented.
The current selected file and loaded diff are identified.
All major visible control clusters are accounted for before branching into interactions.

phases.title: Primary review flow through changed files and diffs
phases.objective: Exercise the core code-review workflow by traversing changed files and validating diff-view behavior.
key_checks: Click each visible changed file badge target in the tree (stream.ts M, chunker.ts M, index.ts +, upload.spec.ts M) and verify the right pane updates accordingly.
Check whether unchanged files behave differently from changed files when selected.
Toggle between Unified and Split and confirm the same file remains selected and the rendering changes appropriately.
Observe whether diff metadata such as file path and line additions/removals update consistently with selection.
Validate basic affordance of collapse/expand behavior in the tree where folder disclosure indicators are visible.
Assess whether the file-status summary footer (Modified 3, Added 1, Lines changed +128 / -54) aligns with visible file states.
exit_criteria: Most visible modified/new files have been opened and cross-checked against the diff pane.
Both diff modes have been exercised.
Any mismatch between tree selection, diff header, and diff contents has been captured.

phases.title: Agent conversation and request submission flow
phases.objective: Validate the feedback loop between user and agent using the visible composer and auto-apply option.
key_checks: Inspect the conversation area for chronology, readability, and clear distinction between user prompt, agent summary, and timeline events.
Type a safe follow-up request in the reply textarea and submit via Send, first without Auto-apply edits enabled if possible.
Toggle Auto-apply edits and inspect whether the control label, state, and risk are understandable before submission.
Check for any acknowledgment, new message, timeline update, or other visible state change after sending.
Verify whether the form prevents empty or accidental submissions and whether focus management is sensible.
exit_criteria: The composer, checkbox, and send interaction have been exercised.
At least one post-submit state response or lack of response is observed and documented.
Risk around auto-apply behavior is understood.

phases.title: Run controls and adjacent navigation/actions
phases.objective: Probe non-core but high-risk controls that can alter run state or move the user into adjacent sections.
key_checks: Test Interrupt and inspect whether run status, buttons, or timeline update in a comprehensible way.
Test Rerun and observe whether the system clearly signals a restarted run, duplicated history, or reset state.
Inspect Accept all changes for confirmation, reversibility cues, or immediate state changes in tree and diff.
Try Open editor, Connect a repo, and Open in VS Code to see whether they open panels, trigger messages, or dead-end silently.
Click Agent, Inbox, Runs, and Settings to determine whether they switch visible content, selected nav state, or do nothing.
Test the search (⌕) and plus (+) controls in the file-tree header for discoverability and visible results.
exit_criteria: Each major adjacent action has been triggered at least once where safe.
Navigation behavior for the top links is understood as in-page state change or inert placeholder.
Any destructive or high-impact action ambiguity has been captured.

phases.title: Mobile responsiveness and reachability audit
phases.objective: Repeat the most important workflow and action checks on mobile, focusing on density, tapability, and access to all panes and controls.
key_checks: Load the page in mobile viewport and verify whether the three-pane layout collapses, stacks, or requires horizontal scrolling.
Repeat critical path checks: select a changed file, inspect diff, toggle Unified/Split if reachable, and access the reply composer.
Confirm whether Interrupt, Rerun, and Accept all changes remain visible and separable on small screens.
Check the top navigation and utility actions for truncation, overflow, or inability to tap due to the prescan small-target warnings.
Assess whether the tiny controls called out in prescan (nav links, search, plus, auto-apply checkbox, Unified/Split, Send) are realistically usable by touch.
exit_criteria: The primary review flow has been repeated in mobile viewport.
Reachability and tap-target issues for critical controls are documented with examples.
A clear judgment is available on whether mobile supports the essential workflow or merely exposes a cramped desktop UI.

coverage_targets.pages: Fully explore index.html and any in-page states revealed by the visible navigation or action controls.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise nearly all visible controls on the main run view, with priority on changed-file selection, diff mode switching, composer submission, run controls, and adjacent repo/editor/navigation actions.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the core review-and-respond workflow plus the highest-risk controls on mobile viewport, emphasizing pane access, overflow, and small tap-target usability.

notes: Do not assume hidden dialogs, backend success states, or extra pages beyond what interactions reveal.
Because the site is a local demo fixture, lack of deep external integration for repo/editor actions should be treated as a UX observation rather than a hard failure unless the UI misleads users.
If destructive actions appear irreversible, prioritize observing confirmation and feedback rather than repeatedly invoking them.

observation.visible_text: Forge / atlas-cli ⌥ feat/streaming-uploads Agent Inbox Runs Settings Connect a repo Open in VS Code RT ATLAS-CLI ⌕ + src upload › stream.ts M › chunker.ts M › retry.ts › index.ts + commands core main.ts test upload.spec.ts M retry.spec.ts auth.spec.ts docs package.json tsconfig.json README.md Modified 3 Added 1 Lines changed +128 / -54 Run #243 · agent is working · 4m 12s elapsed ⏸ Interrupt ↻ Rerun Streaming multipart uploads keep failing on slow connections. Resumes after a network drop just re-upload the whole file. Implement chunked resumable uploads (5 MiB chunks), persist progress to .forge/state.json, and write tests. Don't touch the auth flow. FC I scoped the work to src/upload/ and skimmed the existing stream module. Plan: Split stream.ts: extract a new chunker.ts for chunk-boundary logic (pure functions, easy to test). Add a ChunkedUpload class in index.ts that consults .forge/state.json on start and writes after each chunk. Wire backoff using the existing retry.ts — it already has the right shape. Write tests in test/upload.spec.ts covering: fresh upload, resume mid-stream, retry on 5xx, abort on 4xx. Continuing. 📖 Reading src/upload/stream.ts 208 lines · stable interface 3m 58s ago 📖 Reading src/upload/retry.ts and test/retry.spec.ts retry exponent base = 2, jitter ≤ 250ms — fine to reuse 3m 41s ago ✎ Edited src/upload/stream.ts −47 / +12 — extracted chunker 2m 58s ago ✎ Created src/upload/chunker.ts +86 — pure chunk-boundary helpers 2m 31s ago ✎ Created src/upload/index.ts (ChunkedUpload class) +184 — start/resume/abort lifecycle, persists to .forge/state.json 1m 49s ago ✎ Edited test/upload.spec.ts +102 — four new cases 1m 09s ago ▶ Running pnpm test test/upload.spec.ts 5 of 8 cases · abort-on-4xx passed 23s Suggest, then ask the agent to apply: Auto-apply edits Send src/upload/chunker.ts +86 / −0 Open editor Accept all changes Unified Split @@ -0,0 +1,86 @@ src/upload/chunker.ts + import { Readable } from "stream"; + + export const DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024; + + export interface Chunk { + index: number; + start: number; + end: number; // exclusive + etag?: string; + uploaded?: boolean; + } + + export function planChunks(byteLength: number, chunkSize = DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE): Chunk[] { + if (byteLength <= 0) return []; + const out: Chunk[] = []; + let i = 0, offset = 0; + while (offset < byteLength) { + const end = Math.min(byteLength, offset + chunkSize); + out.push({ index: i, start: offset, end }); + offset = end; i++; + } + return out; + } + + export function mergeProgress(plan: Chunk[], known: Chunk[]): Chunk[] { + const map = new Map(known.map(k => [k.index, k])); + return plan.map(p => ({ ...p, ...(map.get(p.index) ?? {}) })); + } + + export function nextChunk(plan: Chunk[]): Chunk | null { + for (const c of plan) if (!c.uploaded) return c; + return null; + } + + export async function* sliceReadable(src: Readable, plan: Chunk[]) { + const buf: Buffer[] = []; + let bytesQueued = 0; + let cursor = 0; + for await (const piece of src) { + buf.push(piece); + bytesQueued += piece.length; + while (cursor < plan.length && bytesQueued >= plan[cursor].end) { + const need = plan[cursor].end - plan[cursor].start; + const joined = Buffer.concat(buf, bytesQueued); + yield { chunk: plan[cursor], body: joined.subarray(plan[cursor].start, plan[cursor].end) }; + cursor++; + } + } + } ✓ Type-checked clean (tsc) ✓ ESLint — no new warnings ▶ Tests: 5 / 8 — run in progress

Resumes after a network drop just re-upload the whole file. Implement chunked resumable uploads (5 MiB chunks), persist progress to .forge/state.json, and write tests. Don't touch the auth flow.
